title: Training Grounds, the release: the set ships to the normal game as the newest set
notes: The Training Grounds set ships (R1420, R2194000) as the newest set (R1371): its 40 cards, the token TG #39.1 and the 20 Core snapshots TG #41–#60 join every pool that names no set, the deck builder, the Almanac, packs, its set track, random decks and the AI's own decks (part 10, #2203, gates none of it). The owner wrapped the set into Stinkyscape's v0.5 line (R2204000), so the release is a patch of that line and not a major. Its mechanics are the rulings of parts 1–9 (#2194–#2202). A deck holds a Core card or its snapshot, never both (R2195000); a pool keeps both, and one offer, a catalog Discover or Core #97 Zephyrs' top three, shows at most one of a pair (R2204001). Core #95, Classic+ #73, Meditative #95, Stinkyscape #150 and #151, S #149 Wildar and S #4.6 The Big Crunch link TG #39, the edition their texts name (R279), and The Big Crunch casts it sixth (R2200004). Every card of an earlier set whose pool names no set (the random Calls to Chaos, Core #82 KY's Trial's Discover among seven sets, the random Legendaries, Tribute cards and the like, R380) can now offer the set's cards; their texts do not change, and the release claims them as Stinkyscape's did. The account statistics cap is 131,072 bytes (R1142000).

player.title: Training Grounds
new: The Training Grounds set: 40 cards, a token and 20 Core cards made again as Training Grounds cards join the deck builder, the Almanac, packs, random decks and every card pool that names no set.
A deck holds a Core card or its Training Grounds copy, never both.
Training Grounds is the newest set: its track, its ribbon and "More cards from the newest set" lean on it.
changes: Call to Chaos, The Big Crunch, Wildar and every card that picks from a pool of every set can now offer or cast Training Grounds cards.
A Discover never offers a Core card and its Training Grounds copy together.
